2.  WHAT THE PUBLIC CONTEXT READER EXPOSES — AND WHAT IT OMITS
==============================================================

  There is exactly ONE public aggregate reader on a context:
    DERIVATION-RESOLUTION-CONTEXT-BOUND-REFERENCES

  It returns (ROLE REFERENCE) per binding.  The bound VALUE — the cdr of
  the stored cell — is dropped.

── reader output — context A
    (:SCHEMA id(ns=["lisp-plus-form1"],path=["ref","schema","s"]))
    (:CONCLUSION id(ns=["lisp-plus-form1"],path=["ref","conclusion","c"]))
    (:SUPPORT id(ns=["lisp-plus-form1"],path=["ref","support","w1"]))
    (:RECEIVER id(ns=["lisp-plus-form1"],path=["ref","receiver","r"]))

── reader output — context B
    (:SCHEMA id(ns=["lisp-plus-form1"],path=["ref","schema","s"]))
    (:CONCLUSION id(ns=["lisp-plus-form1"],path=["ref","conclusion","c"]))
    (:SUPPORT id(ns=["lisp-plus-form1"],path=["ref","support","w1"]))
    (:RECEIVER id(ns=["lisp-plus-form1"],path=["ref","receiver","r"]))

── the comparison
  entry count A / B                    : 4 / 4
  role+reference lists, element-wise   : IDENTICAL

  EXPOSED : role · reference identifier
  OMITTED : the bound live object, and any durable declaration of
            what that object was intended to denote.  There is no
            such declaration to omit — the layer never asked for one.

  CONSEQUENCE: from the public surface, contexts A and B are
  INDISTINGUISHABLE.  Nothing a durable record can hold separates them.

===============================

  :CONCLUSION  ref/conclusion/c               :volume-reshelved PLUT-7      :volume-reshelved PLUT-7  [equal, distinct objects]
  :SUPPORT     ref/support/w1                 #S(DURABLE-IDENTITY :DOMAIN RECEIPT :NAME witness-1)  #S(DURABLE-IDENTITY :DOMAIN RECEIPT :NAME witness-2)  [DIFFERENT]
  :RECEIVER    ref/receiver/r                 desk over PLUT-7 witness      desk over WRONG-31 witness  [DIFFERENT]

  The support binding is the one that decides the outcome: A's witness

  Two governed acts with OPPOSITE outcomes carry the SAME durable
  submission occurrence identity, and the same durable receipt identity
  where the outcome kind is factored out.  The durable record of a
  governed act does not commit to what its references were declared to
  denote, because no such declaration is required or recorded.

  Honest documentation of this behaviour does not make the identity
  adequate.  This capture is the before-repair witness.
